statement: diagnose precursor limitation before overexpressing terminal pathway enzymes
when a product pathway shares precursors with central carbon metabolism (e.g. PEP, E4P), explicitly evaluate that supply
optimizing central carbon metabolism is often necessary, not optional, for efficient production of precursor-limited products
when a host lacks a native pathway to a target product, prioritize pathway construction over pathway modification
de novo pathway engineering should be paired with host-level optimization of precursor and cofactor supply, not treated as a standalone gene-insertion task
when a product depends on a precursor pool shared with central metabolism, diagnose precursor balance before increasing terminal pathway enzyme expression
rewiring central carbon metabolism, not only terminal pathway enzymes, is sometimes necessary to relieve precursor-driven bottlenecks
